chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is permissible for a man to enjoy (marry) a Jewish woman and a Christian woman, even if he has a free (non-slave) woman.

key_terms.حُرَّةٌ: a free woman (as opposed to a slave)
key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعَ: to enjoy (in the context of marriage, i.e., to take as a wife)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a Muslim man to marry a Jewish or Christian woman if he is already married to another free woman?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that the permissibility of marrying Jewish and Christian women is not restricted by the presence of a free Muslim wife, addressing potential confusion regarding polygyny limits. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of *Kitabiyyat* compared to Muslim women, a key topic in Shia jurisprudence for determining marital eligibility and the number of concurrent wives.
